# On Hilbert's 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation

Nick Polson and Vadim Sokolov. Independently published, 2026. Edition 1, version 1.0.1. DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.23407620](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23407620).

In 1900 David Hilbert asked for a mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics, beginning with probability and mechanics, and for the limiting processes that lead from the atomistic view to the laws of motion of continua. This book follows that program, with Henri Poincaré as a central figure: Kolmogorov's axioms, de Finetti's theorem and Sanov's large deviation theorem; ergodic theory and the method of types; Brownian motion, entropy and Nelson's stochastic mechanics; kinetic theory, Lanford's theorem and the passage from the Boltzmann equation to the Navier Stokes equations.

It then adds the inverse passage, from observed fluids back to the states that produced them. Part IV treats the inverse problem of a partial differential equation as Bayesian estimation on its solution manifold. For linear equations the adjoint evolution of the data is a sufficient statistic; for nonlinear equations it is asymptotically sufficient under a uniform Bernstein von Mises statement that the book states and leaves open. The cost of generative computation depends on the dimension that the data can resolve, and examples and experiments cover the heat, Navier Stokes and Schrödinger equations.

The last part treats inference itself as statistical mechanics: spin systems and Lee Yang zeros, Schrödinger bridges and generative Bayesian computation, gates as approximate nonlinear filters, and the thermodynamics of information. A final chapter lists open problems and builds a bridge to Hilbert's eighth problem through the de Bruijn Newman heat flow. Every chapter closes with exercises, and the Python code behind the computed figures and tables is in the repository.

## Main results

- [Adjoint representation of the sufficient statistic](RESULTS.md#adjoint_representation_of_the_sufficient_statistic) (Lemma 15.1, page 206): For a linear evolution equation that is diagonal in a fixed basis, the data statistic that is sufficient for the initial state is the coefficient vector of the time zero value of the solution of the backward adjoint equation driven by the data as point sources.
- [Exact sufficiency, linear case](RESULTS.md#exact_sufficiency_linear_case) (Proposition 15.2, page 207): In the linear model with a Gaussian prior the adjoint statistic is sufficient, the posterior given it is the full data posterior, and the conditional quantile map is exactly affine with slope equal to the posterior covariance.
- [Equivalence of the one step efficient score summary with the efficient centering](RESULTS.md#equivalence_with_the_efficient_centering) (Proposition 15.5, page 210): Under explicit regularity, rate and Lipschitz conditions, the cross fitted one step efficient score summary agrees with the efficient centering of Nickl's Bernstein von Mises theorem to order smaller than the root N scale in a negative Sobolev norm, so it is a computable center of the Gaussian limit of the posterior.
- [Jiang Wong under a uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption: the posterior mean summary is asymptotically sufficient](RESULTS.md#jiang_wong_under_bernstein_von_mises) (Theorem 15.38, page 256): If a Bernstein von Mises theorem holds uniformly over prior typical truths, then conditioning on the posterior mean alone, or on any summary root N equivalent to it, loses nothing at the root N scale: the recentered posterior given the summary and the recentered posterior given all of the data have the same Gaussian limit in Wasserstein distance. Status: conditional on the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption (Assumption U).
- [Effective dimension under dissipation](RESULTS.md#effective_dimension_under_dissipation) (Theorem 15.46, page 267): For the heat and Stokes equations on the torus with a power law prior, the number of modes in which the data at least halve the prior variance grows like a power of the sample size divided by viscosity times observation time, so dissipation lowers the effective dimension; for a nonlinear forward map, under a uniform Bernstein von Mises hypothesis and assumptions on the training residuals and the summary, a generator need only learn the posterior scale on those modes (in the linear model it needs no training), and the cost of using the prior spread beyond them is bounded explicitly. Status: conditional on Assumption U and other hypotheses of the quantile generator theorem, in part (ii) for nonlinear maps.
- [Transfer of Bernstein von Mises guarantees to the GBC posterior (BvM for GBC)](RESULTS.md#bvm_for_gbc) (Theorem 16.2, page 275): If the posterior produced by a generative Bayesian computation (GBC) generator is closer to the exact posterior than the root N scale in Wasserstein distance and concentrates on the localization set with bounded moments, then it inherits the Bernstein von Mises limit of the exact posterior for the initial condition and, for the reaction diffusion and two dimensional Navier Stokes equations, for the trajectory, with exact asymptotic coverage of its credible bands and, for Navier Stokes, attainment of the local asymptotic minimax bound for bounded losses; nothing is assumed about how the generator was trained.
- [No uniform guarantee: minimax lower bound for conditional quantile generators over monotone Hölder classes](RESULTS.md#no_uniform_guarantee_for_quantile_generators) (Theorem 16.15, page 290): Any generator, trained on M simulated pairs, that must be accurate at a fixed interior summary value for every conditional law in a monotone Hölder class of conditional quantile maps of smoothness beta on a J dimensional summary has, for some map in the class, Wasserstein error at least a constant free of J times (C M) to the power minus beta over (2 beta plus J) with probability at least 1/8, where C bounds the design density, so root N accuracy uniformly over the class requires at least N to the power 1 plus J over (2 beta) simulations divided by C, more than any polynomial once J grows; reading this as the accuracy condition of the transfer theorem uses the uniform Bernstein von Mises assumption.

All 92 catalogued results, with statements and status, are in [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md). To credit a result, cite Polson and Sokolov (2026), *On Hilbert's 6th Problem: Probability, Mechanics and Bayesian Computation*, edition 1, with the number of the result.

## Files

- `pdf/hilbert6.pdf`: the book.
- `source/`: the LaTeX source, bibliography included; the macros are defined in `source/main.tex`.
- `source/code/`: the code that computes the figures and tables.
- `RESULTS.md` and `summaries/`: the catalog of results and one summary per chapter.
- `site/`: what the book's web pages are built from: `book.json` with every fact and result, the book page and the page of the results by chapter in Markdown, their head tags and the book's `llms.txt` section.
- Book page: https://vsokolov.org/books/hilbert6/

## Building

The book: in `source/`, run `pdflatex main.tex` three times. There is no BibTeX step; the bibliography is `source/chapters/bibliography.tex`. The cover: in `source/cover/`, run `pdflatex "\def\InteriorPages{N}\input{cover}"` twice, with N the page count of `source/main.pdf` (`pdfinfo` shows it), since the width of the spine depends on it.

The code: `source/code/` holds the Python 3 scripts that compute the book's figures and tables, with numpy, scipy and matplotlib (two scripts also use PyTorch and two use JAX). Appendix B of the book says which script produces which figure or table and what a rerun gives. `source/code/anc/` holds the code and the recorded results (JSON files) of the experiments of Part IV, with its own `README.txt`; the replicate studies of Chapter 17 ran as Slurm jobs on a cluster (the `.sbatch` files). `source/code/ns_checks/` holds four scripts that measure the corrections of the Navier Stokes experiment of Chapter 17.
